newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China bought 120,000-150,000 tonnes soymeal - trade.
newsitem.headline: China bought 120,000-150,000 tonnes soymeal - trade.

text.p: China late last week bought between 120,000-150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November and December delivery from the United States, South America and India, Hong Kong-based traders said on Monday.
The meal was sold last Thursday or Friday and was mainly from the United States, but some was also from South America and India, the grain traders said.
The price was said to be below $305 per tonne, c and f China, for the U.S.-origin meal.
One trader added that at least two cargoes of about 10,000 tonnes each of Indian soymeal were sold to China last week.
Thousands of tonnes of meal arriving at the same time in China towards the end of the year would drive domestic prices down, trade sources said.
"So many arrivals at the same time will collapse the market easily," one trader said.
While meal was in demand last week, this week beans would top the agenda, another trader said.

"This week, especially today, more people are enquiring about beans," the source said, noting that Chinese crushers were looking for material in the new financial year and that prices around $310 c and f China were being discussed with buyers.
Enquiries for both soybeans and meal had shot up after the price drop on the Chicago Board of Trade, a China-based trader said.
Forecasts for an active harvest weekend and aggressive fund selling knocked CBOT soybean futures sharply lower with November closing at $7.27-1/4 per bushel on Friday.
Soy meal closed $2.50-$4.00 per ton lower, with October down $3.70 at $244.10.
